newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Central bank brakes Mauritius rupee's weakening.
newsitem.headline: Central bank brakes Mauritius rupee's weakening.

text.p: A central bank intervention put breaks on the Mauritian rupee's weakening against the dollar on Thursday, commercial banks forex dealers said.

The rupee was fixed slightly weaker against the dollar at a mean commercial rate of 20.1265 from 20.1234 on Wednesday. Versus the pound, the rupee was quoted at a mean of 32.538 from 32.369 on Wednesday.
Forex dealers said a central bank intervention on Wednesday supported the rupee by offsetting a stronger dollar in overnight international markets.
"The central bank sold dollars during the intervention at 20.08 rupees to the dollar which was lower than the interbank rate," one dealer said.
The net effect of the intervention and the stronger overnight dollar, was little changed rupee, the dealer added.
Wednesday's central bank market intervention was the second one in the week. On Tuesday, the bank also sold dollars at a rate lower than the prevailing interbank rate, dealers said.
With such regular central bank interventions, activity in the local interbank forex market is presently low, they added.
"The interventions are offering better rates than you can get from interbank. So (commercial) banks prefer to wait for the central bank," the dealer said.
